subject.title: feat(sqlite): dedicated quarantine store survives primary database damage

question: Should OpenClaw make a separate SQLite file the authoritative quarantine record and intentionally fail open when that file cannot be read?
rationale: This is an operational persistence and availability policy choice, not a mechanical correction: it introduces a new durable artifact and chooses availability over quarantine enforcement when that artifact itself is unavailable.

options.title: Approve the dedicated-store contract
options.body: Accept the separate quarantine database and documented fail-open behavior after reviewing direct damaged-state restart proof.

options.title: Require fail-closed quarantine reads
options.body: Keep corruption protection strict by refusing opens whenever an existing quarantine store cannot be read, accepting broader availability impact.

options.title: Rework the persistence approach
options.body: Reject the new standalone store and choose a different recovery boundary before further implementation work.

recommendation.title: Approve the dedicated-store contract
recommendation.body: Accept the separate quarantine database and documented fail-open behavior after reviewing direct damaged-state restart proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged quarantine design that this PR revises and are the clearest available routing candidate from the supplied history.
